 J U D G M E N T
This claim petition under Sec.166 of MV Act 1989 is filed by injured boy through his natural guardian seeking compensation of .8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. Petitioner has stated that on 08082019 about 400 p.m. he was returning to his house by riding the bicycle via Ambedkar Nagar towards Prashanth Layout, on Whitefield Main road, near Royal mart, Bengaluru, the driver of autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AA2198 (herein after called as offending vehicle), drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Petitioner's bicycle.
As a result, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to Vydehi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient and spent more than .1,00,000/ towards medical and other incidental expenses.
The accident was due rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 14 years and was studying in 10th standard.
Due to the accidental injuries he was unable to attend the class the cannot participate in co curricular activities and it affects his future career.

Petitioner claims that the Respondents being the owner and insurer of the alleged offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest at 12% from the date of filing of the petition.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and she was placed exparte.
4. The Respondent No.2Insurance company has filed written statement by denying the petition averments.

It has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of alleged offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6)of MV Act.
It has further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid driving licence and it had no valid fitness certificate as on the date of accident.

It has denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner,
treatment taken by him, expenses claimed by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.
For all these reasons, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above, the following Issues arise for my consideration :-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 08082019 about 4.00 p.m. when he was riding bicycle, on Whitefield Main road, near Royal Mart, Bengaluru District, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing No.KA 03AA2198 drove it in high speed and rash and negligently dashed against the Petitioner's bicycle due to which the Petitioner fell Adith.S vs Sabiha Banu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182455464/
2 down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3 . What order ?

6. In order to prove the claim, the natural guardian/mother of Petitioner is examined as PW.1, the doctor who has assessed the disability of Petitioner is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
7.

The Respondent No.2 has examined the SDA, RTO, K.R.Puram as RW1 and ASI, Whitefield Traffic PS is examined as RW2 and its official is examined as RW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to 6 respectively.
8. I have heard the counsel for Petitioner and perused the material on record.

9. By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 10. ISSUE NO.1: Since the Petitioner being minor, represented by his natural guardian/mother and she is examined as PW1.
PW1 has stated that the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of the autorickshaw.

PW1 has stated in her affidavit of chiefexamination that on 08 08 2019 about 400 p.m. her son was returning to home by riding the bicycle via Ambedkar Nagar towards Prashanth Layout, on Whitefield Main road, near Royal mart, Bengaluru, the driver of autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA03AA2198 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the bicycle.
As a result, her son fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11. The grand mother of Petitioner gave first information statement to the Police as per Ex.P.2 on the basis of which Ex.P.1 FIR was registered.
Spot Mahazar and sketch was done by the Police as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
The offending vehicle was inspected as per IMV report at Ex.P.5.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet is filed by the concerned Police as per Ex.P.6.
Ex.P.7 is the wound certificate, which shows that the Petitioner has sustained left hand compound extensor tendon injury.
12. The RespondentInsurance company alleges that it was the negligence of petitioner himself who went without observing the other vehicles and dashed the autorickshaw.
PW1 mother of the petitioner denied the same and contended that it was not his negligence.

Except this suggestion,
Respondent has not produced any other documentary or oral evidence.

Even the investigating Adith.S vs Sabiha Banu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182455464/
3 officer is examined as RW2, but nothing has been suggested or asked about the negligence of Petitioner.
After the investigation police have filed charge sheet against the drive of the autorickshaw.
All the medical and police records corroborate with the petition averments and it appears to be negligence on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
The Petitioner has succeeded in proving the negligence of the driver of the offending autorickshaw and hence Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

13. ISSUE NO.2 :The Petitioner was of 14 years old at the time of accident and has sustained Left hand compound extensor tendon injury He was admitted to Vydehi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 08082019 to 14082019 as per Ex.P11.
PW2 doctor has stated that on 11052022 he examined the Petitioner to assess the disability.

He has gone through the wound certificate and discharge summary and found that the Petitioner has sustained Left hand compound extensor tendon injury for which he has undergone wound debridement and extensor tendon repair and after discharge he has attended the followup treatment.
Recent Xray of left hand showed normal study.
Further, PW2 has stated that now the Petitioner complains of weakness and pain in the left hand, loss of sensation over the dorsum of the left hand.
So far as the disability is concerned the doctor has given the total physical disability of the left hand at 27% and 9% to the whole body.

Along with his evidence, PW2 has produced clinical notes and Xray at Ex.P.14 and 15.
14.
As it is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court it is difficult to assess the compensation in the case of children sufferings from disability on account of motor vehicle accident.
The doctor has stated that the total whole body disability is at 9%.
In the crossexamination of PW2, he has admitted that Petitioner is of younger age and the fractures are united.
He denied the suggestion that there cannot be any disability to the Petitioner since he is of younger age and restrictions or difficulties will reduce with age.

15. Considering the tender age of the Petitioner and nature of injuries sustained by him, type of treatment obtained and also considering the evidence of doctor, the permanent functional disability to the whole body is considered as 7%.
16.
There are no materials to show that the Petitioner has lost his educational career due to the present accident and hence loss of education due to accidental injuries is not considered.

PW1 has produced the study certificate at Ex.P.14, issued by Department of Industrial Training and employment, which shows that now the Petitioner is studying in Trade of Mechanic (Motor vehicle)
from November 2021.

sentences.text: 17. As held in the Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396 if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, the compensation should be .3 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be .1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.

In the present case though the whole body disability is 10%, nature of injuries, age of Petitioner is taken into consideration and considering that the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court was of the 2013 and the accident had occurred in the present case in the year 2019.
Considering that the age of the Petitioner, I deem it proper to award .1,50,000/ for Adith.S vs Sabiha Banu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182455464/

4 Pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock,
hardship, inconvenience and discomforts, etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.
Under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization .25,000/ is awarded.
18. For the medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization the Petitioner has produced medical bills amounting to .1,06,352/ at Ex.P.9.
Respondent has disputed the medical bills.

On perusal of entire medical bills and excluding the advance receipts after considering IP bill,
the total medical bills produced by the Petitioner are for .24,873/ only.
Hence, by considering medical bills, .25,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner towards medical expenses.

19. By considering the above judgment, and taking into consideration of all the materials produced by the Petitioner, this tribunal awards compensation under the following heads:
Sl. HEAD COMPENSATION No.
1. Pain and suffering .1,50,000/ already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2. Discomfort, inconvenience . 25,000/ and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization 3. Medical and incidental .
expenses
20. Liability:

The Respondentinsurance company has denied its liability only on the ground that the driver of the offending autorickshaw was not possessing valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and it was the violation of the condition of the policy.
21. Respondent No.1 RC owner has remained exparte.
Insurance company examined official from RTO, KR Puram, Bengaluru as RW1.
He has produced DL extract of driver of autorickshaw.
According to which his DL was not renewed from 2009.
The IO is examined as RW2 and he admits after confronting DL extract that the accused driver had no DL as on the date of accident.
He admits that he should have invoked Section for not holding DL by the accused while filing chargesheet.
IO says that he had issued notice U/s.133 of MV Act and obtained reply.
He produced copies at Ex.R.3 and 4.
Ex.R.4 reply shows same DL number as in Ex.R.2 DL extract.
But it is not renewed.
It appears that IO has not verified the original DL.

22. Insurance company examined its official as RW3 and based on the DL extract and other records, he has deposed that the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in view of violation of terms of insurance contract.
23. In the present case admittedly insurance covers the third party risk.
The insurance policy is a contract executed between the owner and the insurer.

In the present case though the insurance was Adith.S vs Sabiha Banu on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182455464/
5 valid as on the date of accident the owner allowed the driver knowingly that he did not possess any valid driving licence.
It is the willful breach of terms of contract of insurance.
24. Petitioner requested to order for pay and recovery as it is the case of injury to third party and the respondent No.1 is placed exparte.

25. By considering the Judgments in The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Annemma W/O Late Iranna Javalgi dated 231120171, ICICI Lombord General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt. T. Padma &
another2, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. M.S. Raghu & another 3,

sentences.text: Considering the available materials on record, and since it is the third party liability, by following the decision of full bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court, First Respondent RC owner is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the 2nd respondent insurance company i.e. insurer of the autorickshaw is directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner i.e., Respondent No.1 in view of breach of contract of insurance.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

26. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given 1 2018(1) AKR 701 - AIR Karnataka Reporter 2 MFA 1165/2010 dated 09.07.2019 3 MFA 384/2010 dated 28.06.2011 to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .2,00,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1RC owner is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner.

Respondent No.2 shall deposit aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this Order and recover the entire compensation amount along with interest from the Respondent No.1 in view of violation of terms of policy.

On said deposit, Rs.1,00,000/ of the compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through Epayment and remaining amount of Rs.1,00,000/
shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice till he attains the age of majority.
The guardian is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
24. Petitioner requested to order for pay and recovery as it is the case of injury to third party and the respondent No.1 is placed exparte.
Considering the available materials on record, and since it is the third party liability, by following the decision of full bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court, First Respondent RC owner is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the 2nd respondent insurance company i.e. insurer of the autorickshaw is directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner i.e., Respondent No.1 in view of breach of contract of insurance.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

O R D E R Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .2,00,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1RC owner is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this Order and recover the entire compensation amount along with interest from the Respondent No.1 in view of violation of terms of policy.
On said deposit, Rs.1,00,000/ of the compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through Epayment and remaining amount of Rs.1,00,000/
shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice till he attains the age of majority.
The guardian is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
